newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares stable but unconvinced by Wall St.
newsitem.headline: German shares stable but unconvinced by Wall St.

text.p: German shares were treading water in late dealings on Tuesday as the scale of the rebound on Wall Street from Monday's lows helped support the German market but still failed to inject new optimism.
"It's just not enough," said a dealer of a gain of some 0.5 percent on the Dow Jones Index at around 1447 GMT.
"People were pretty convinced Monday was a one-off."
The 30-share IBIS DAX index was up 5.19 points at 3,753.42 points, off an intraday low of 3,709.58 but also well below a high of 3,775.08 hit in the early afternoon.
September DTB DAX futures were up 3.5 at 3,782.0.

Trading was highly selective with almost all attention focused in the afternoon on banking giant Deutsche Bank AG and electronics and engineering group Siemens AG, both of which were lifted strongly by what dealers said were strong technical buy signals.
Deutsche was up 4.10 marks, or more than four percent, at 101.65 marks while Siemens was up 2.6 percent at 106.30 marks.
Dealers said there was no fundamental reason for interest in either share but both were attracting buyers once they passed the 100-mark level.
More broadly, Wall Street would lead the way, dealers said.
